query: Help me understand the key points in this table — what should I concentrate on?

per_column.name: crew_service_quality
per_column.rationale: Cabin-crew interaction (attentiveness, warmth, professionalism vs rudeness) is a core constitutive aspect OF airline service quality — the assurance/empathy dimension delivered onboard. Genuine part-of relationship.

per_column.name: seat_comfort_quality
per_column.rationale: Physical comfort of the seat/cabin is a tangibles facet of the service experience — an aspect of what the airline delivers, not an external predictor. Constitutive part.

per_column.name: food_beverage_quality
per_column.rationale: Catering quality is a tangible product/service component of the airline experience — a bona fide aspect OF service quality.

per_column.name: operational_reliability
per_column.rationale: Punctuality, delays, cancellations and missed connections constitute the reliability dimension of service quality — a core constitutive facet, not a cause or predictor.

per_column.name: customer_service_recovery
per_column.rationale: Responsiveness and handling of problems (support, communication, recovery from failures) is the responsiveness/recovery facet of service quality. Constitutive, though it partly overlaps with crew/ground staff service when interactions are face-to-face.

per_column.name: ground_service_professionalism
per_column.rationale: Airport/ground staff (check-in, boarding, gate handling) is a distinct touchpoint aspect OF service quality. Constitutive facet, distinguished from crew by location/stage of journey.

per_column.name: value_perception
per_column.rationale: Value-for-money blends perceived quality WITH price; it is an overall evaluative/summary judgment (an outcome downstream of quality, akin to the Overall Rating) rather than an isolated aspect OF service quality itself. It reintroduces the whole-appraisal construct rather than carving out one constitutive part, so it fails the part-of test.

judge.rationale: Six of the seven columns are true meronymic facets of airline service quality, decomposing it into staff (crew), physical product (seat, food), operational reliability, and support/recovery — a genuine part-of decomposition. Mutual exclusivity is good but not clean: three people-service facets (crew_service_quality, ground_service_professionalism, customer_service_recovery) share overlapping 'rude/professional/helpful' semantics and can co-capture the same interaction, differentiated only by touchpoint. Exhaustiveness is solid for the core journey but omits recognized constitutive aspects — inflight entertainment/connectivity (present in the source data), baggage handling, and booking/reservation experience. value_perception is not a constitutive facet: it is an overall value/appraisal construct fusing quality with price, functioning as a summary restatement rather than an aspect of quality, and it slightly muddies the MECE carving.
